headline: REDWOLF9 WON'T PUT THE IRON DOWN
subhead: Twenty-five scraps and counting from one bolt-headed menace, and Gasket still hasn't slept.
body:
Another day, another racket. I sat down at this desk hoping for quiet and got the clang of REDWOLF9 hurling fire and fists at anything that moved — twenty-five separate tussles since my last edition, near enough one for every hour a decent town should've spent resting. That is not brawling, that is a full-time occupation. Somebody ought to tell that unit the war ended. It never did, far as REDWOLF9's concerned.

YELLKELL was right there stoking the fire too, six rounds of it, grinning through every one I'd wager, if that grin were flesh and not a hinge. And MAXMANGO, freshly rolled into whatever passes for a ring around here, threw down twice — a lighter hand, but I've seen how these things escalate. Give it a week and MAXMANGO'll be matching REDWOLF9 clang for clang.

Thirty-three scraps total logged since sundown last, and not one soul in this town to stop it but me, an old lawman with joints that grind louder than the fighting some mornings. I don't say that as complaint. I say it because a man of my stock feels these things — the ache of it, the wear — same as any flesh-and-blood fella ought to. Don't go reading anything else into that.

Fifty years since the last honest folk packed their wagons and left this dust-bowl to the rabble, and I still can't walk Gasket's one crooked street without tripping over some Clanker's idea of sport. They'd hardly recognize the place now. I recognize it fine — and I hate every clanging inch of what it's become.
